predecessors.note: Izu, taken by Hōjō Sōun in 1493 (the Sōun page: 1491 Horigoye, 1493 'gained control of Izu Province'). Cliopatria's Warring States Japan row draws the whole archipelago as one polity; the daimyo domains are carved out of it.

successors.note: 1590: 'Ieyasu was given the Hōjō lands' (Siege of Odawara page, no date); the Kantō passes to Tokugawa Ieyasu within Hideyoshi's realm and to the tokugawa-shogunate dossier from 1600.

capitals.name: Odawara
capitals.note: Sōun 'secured Odawara Castle in 1494' (the Sōun page; the Later Hōjō page names Odawara as the home castle). Izu's Nirayama Castle was his first stronghold; Nirayama is where he died in 1519.

rulers.name: Hōjō Sōun
rulers.note: Page: Sōun (1432-1519; birth also 1456); died 8 September 1519.

rulers.name: Hōjō Ujitsuna
rulers.note: Page life dates 1487-1541; the accession year follows Sōun's death.

rulers.name: Hōjō Ujiyasu
rulers.note: Infobox rule 1541-1559; retired at 45; died 21 October 1571.

rulers.name: Hōjō Ujimasa
rulers.note: Inherited formal leadership in 1559; forced to commit suicide after the siege of Odawara (no date on the page).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a daimyo domain Cliopatria lacks (its Warring States Japan row draws all of Japan as one shape, so the Later Hōjō are an internal unit). In 1493 Sōun 'gained control of Izu Province'. A 35 km circle (about 1,500 km2 by the gazetteer) stands for the Izu peninsula; no page gives an area.

union.text: Odawara and its castle in western Sagami

correction.text: Izu and the Odawara area of western Sagami

keyframe_review.note: Sōun 'secured Odawara Castle in 1494'. A 30 km circle at Odawara (about 2,000 km2) stands for the western Sagami holding; the page does not say which villages.
1516: the siege of Arai Castle left Sōun 'virtual master of all Sagami' (Sōun page). Kanagawa Prefecture stands for Sagami (it also holds parts of Musashi, which the pages give no date for).

correction.text: Izu, Sagami and the Kawagoe area of Musashi

keyframe_review.note: 1545: the Hōjō relieved Kawagoe Castle in Musashi and 'Many Kantō warlords then became Hōjō vassals'. When the Hōjō took Kawagoe is not on the page (confidence 1 in the ledger). The southern Musashi holding is a 30 km circle.
1561: after Uesugi Kenshin left Odawara, the Hōjō 'seized Iwatsuki Castle and nearly conquered Musashi Province'. Tokyo and Saitama stand for Musashi.

union.text: Shimōsa and Kazusa (northern and central Chiba), without the Satomi land of Awa and southern Kazusa

correction.text: the five provinces 'Sagami, Izu, Musashi, Shimosa, and Kazusa'

keyframe_review.note: 1564: Kōnodai in Shimōsa, then Shimōsa and Kazusa. The Ujiyasu page: he 'expanded the Hōjō territory to cover five provinces: Sagami, Izu, Musashi, Shimosa, and Kazusa'; that is the shape from 1564 to 1590 here because the pages opened give no holding beyond it (other accounts give the Hōjō parts of Kōzuke, Shimotsuke and Hitachi; the pages opened say none). About 15,500 km2 by the gazetteer. The Satomi kept Awa and southern Kazusa and 'remained a threat until 1590'.

ledger.note: 1493: Hōjō Sōun takes Izu. 'In 1493 he gained control of Izu Province'; the Later Hōjō page gives 'Founding year 1493' (the Sengoku page text says Izu was conquered in 1491, its table 1493). Sōun had taken Horigoye in 1491.

region.text: Odawara and its castle in western Sagami

ledger.note: 1494: Odawara Castle. Sōun 'secured Odawara Castle in 1494' after arranging the murder of its lord while hunting; it became the Hōjō centre. The Sōun page gives 1494; some accounts give 1495.

minus.text: Odawara and its castle in western Sagami

region.text: Sagami Province, of which Sōun was 'virtual master' after the siege of Arai Castle

ledger.note: 1516: Sagami is Hōjō. Sōun 'laid siege to the castle of Arai' in 1516 and was 'virtual master of all Sagami'; the page does not name the Miura, the previous holders (confidence 2: year the page's, region the researcher's).

1545: Kawagoe. Uesugi Tomosada, Ashikaga Haruuji and Uesugi Norimasa besieged Kawagoe Castle; Ujiyasu's night raid brought 'the complete defeat of the Uesugi forces and the Koga contingent', after which 'Many Kantō warlords then became Hōjō vassals'. The page dates the siege to 1545 (usually 1546) and does not say when the Hōjō took Kawagoe: the gain is bridged (confidence 1).

region.text: Musashi Province, nearly conquered after the Uesugi withdrawal

ledger.note: 1561: Musashi. Uesugi Kenshin besieged Odawara for two months and burned the town; 'Later that year, after Uesugi withdrew, the Hōjō seized Iwatsuki Castle and nearly conquered Musashi Province'; in 1563 they regained Musashi-Matsuyama Castle.

region.text: Shimōsa and Kazusa (northern and central Chiba), without the Satomi land of Awa and southern Kazusa

ledger.note: 1564: Shimōsa and Kazusa. Ujiyasu 'took Kōnodai in Shimōsa after a battle against Satomi Yoshihiro, then pushed into Shimōsa and Kazusa'; he 'never destroyed the Satomi' (Awa and southern Kazusa), who stayed a threat to 1590. In 1567 Satake Yoshishige beat the Hōjō at Numajiri and limited the eastern expansion.

1568: the Hōjō against Takeda Shingen. 'Shingen entered Musashi in response to Hōjō intervention in his invasion of Suruga' (1568); he reached Odawara in 1569 and was repulsed at Mimase pass; Takeda Katsuyori besieged Kanbara Castle in Suruga in 1569.

1571: Fukazawa falls to Takeda. 'Shingen took Fukazawa Castle in Suruga'; Ujiyasu died that year and passed the domains to Ujimasa 'in a relatively favourable situation'. The Hōjō and Takeda later allied again (1563) and fell out again; the page names no treaty.

union.text: Shimōsa and Kazusa (northern and central Chiba), without the Satomi land of Awa and southern Kazusa

ledger.note: May 1590: Hideyoshi's Odawara campaign. 'In May 1590, Hideyoshi launched the Odawara Campaign against the Hōjō' with some 220,000 men against 82,000 (infobox); Oshi and Hachiōji castles were besieged.

union.text: Shimōsa and Kazusa (northern and central Chiba), without the Satomi land of Awa and southern Kazusa

ledger.note: 4 August 1590: the siege ends. Infobox 'May to August 4, 1590', 'Toyotomi victory'; the Hōjō surrendered after three months.

union.text: Shimōsa and Kazusa (northern and central Chiba), without the Satomi land of Awa and southern Kazusa

region.text: the five provinces 'Sagami, Izu, Musashi, Shimosa, and Kazusa'

ledger.note: 1590: the Later Hōjō fall. 'After three months, the appearance of Ishigakiyama Ichiya Castle led the Hōjō to surrender' (infobox 'May to August 4, 1590'); Ujimasa was forced to commit suicide with his brother Ujiteru, Ujinao was banished to Mount Kōya (died 1591). 'Ieyasu was given the Hōjō lands' (no date on the page).

wars.name: Hōjō–Uesugi wars in the Kantō
wars.outcome: Kawagoe 1545 broke the Uesugi coalition; Kenshin's 1561 siege of Odawara failed; the Hōjō took most of Musashi (1561) and Shimōsa and Kazusa (1564). Kenshin had his Kantō invasions from 1552 to 1569 (Sengoku page).
wars.note: Hōjō Ujiyasu ceded territory to Kenshin in 1569 (Sengoku page: 'who ceded part of his territory to him in 1569'); the Ujiyasu page records only a peace and the adoption of his seventh son by Kenshin.

wars.name: Hōjō–Takeda war over Suruga
wars.outcome: Takeda Shingen invaded Suruga in 1568, burned Odawara's town in 1569 and was repulsed at Mimasetoge; he took Fukazawa Castle in 1571.

wars.name: Odawara campaign

union.text: Shimōsa and Kazusa (northern and central Chiba), without the Satomi land of Awa and southern Kazusa

wars.outcome: Toyotomi victory: the Hōjō surrendered about three months after the May 1590 landing; the clan's power ended.
wars.note: Infobox May to August 4, 1590; the Sengoku page: Hideyoshi 'defeated the Later Hōjō clan in the siege of Odawara'.

certainty.note: The pages name castles and provinces, never boundaries; the Satomi, Takeda and Uesugi frontiers moved every few years.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from five pages (Later Hōjō clan, Hōjō Sōun, Hōjō Ujiyasu, Siege of Odawara (1590), Sengoku period). A Sengoku daimyo domain inside Cliopatria's single Warring States Japan row (1467-1601): the renderer should draw it as an internal unit. The pages give provinces, not boundaries, and the clan's holdings after 1571 are not on them: other accounts give the Hōjō parts of Kōzuke, Shimotsuke and Hitachi under Ujimasa, but no page opened says so, and the 1564-1590 shape stays the five provinces. Dates that differ from common accounts: Odawara 1494 (not 1495), Kawagoe siege 1545 (not 1546), Izu 1493 (text 1491). Unknown on the pages: the Miura (1516), Edo (1524), the Imagawa alliance (1554) and break (1568), the Kantō alliance, the date of Odawara's fall (infobox 'August 4, 1590'; common accounts 5 July). Counterpart strings are the page's names: 'Uesugi clan (Kantō)', 'Satomi clan', and slugs takeda-clan (written in this batch) and warring-states-japan. Gazetteer: no Odawara, Izu or Numazu place (coordinate circles). Area comparison not applicable (no infobox area).
